newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China North warns affiliates on misconduct.
newsitem.headline: China North warns affiliates on misconduct.

text.p: China North Industrial Group, a major state-owned conglomerate, has warned its listed affiliates not to speculate in shares and vowed to impose severe penalties on violators, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Wednesday.

The Beijing-based group controls more than 150 enterprises across the country, involved in a wide range of products including munitions, machinery and chemicals, a company official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.

The company, which includes amongst its subsidiaries arms merchant China North Industries Corp (Norinco), has controlling stakes in four firms listed on the Shenzhen or Shanghai stock exchanges, some directly and others in the names of other companies.
They are Chongqing Changan Automobile Co Ltd, Motorcycle maker China Jialing Industrial Co Ltd, Shenzhen North Jianshe Motorcycle Co Ltd and Chengdu Tianxing Instrument and Meter Co Ltd.
In a circular issued to the listed firms, China North ordered them to comply strictly with Beijing's ban on public companies entering the country's stock market, the newspaper said.
In its latest clampdown against stock speculation, Beijing recently sacked the heads of several domestic brokerages, listed firms and banks.

Earlier this month, Beijing fired He Yun, the president of Shenzhen Development Bank Ltd, China's only bank with a domestic listing, after the bank was found to have used bank funds to trade its own shares.
Norinco was implicated in the largest arms smuggling case in United States history last year and several employees of the company were sentenced by a Chinese court to jail terms in May.
